note.text: Economics examines choices about scarce resources and the production, distribution and use of goods and services. A want is a desire for something; resources are means used to satisfy wants. Scarcity means resources are limited relative to the wants they could satisfy. It affects rich as well as poor people. Because not every want can be met at once, people rank alternatives and choose. A school, household or government also faces choices about time, land, labour and materials.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Economics examines choices about scarce resources and the production, distribution and use of goods and services. A want is a desire for something; resources are means used to satisfy wants. Scarcity means resources are limited relative to the wants they could satisfy. It affects rich as well as poor people. Because not every want can be met at once, people rank alternatives and choose. A school, household or government also faces choices about time, land, labour and materials.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Bih has one free afternoon. She wants to revise, help at a stall and visit a friend. Even if no money changes hands, time is scarce. A school in Buea may have enough land for a garden or an extra play area but not both on the same plot. Economics asks how such choices are made and what must be given up.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the decision maker, the resource constraint and the alternatives. Do not define scarcity simply as having no money: a well-funded club may still lack time or space. Explain the connection: limited resources in relation to wants make choice necessary.
